positions.title: Researcher in Computer Science
positions.locationName: Inter-Networking Research Group, University of California, Santa Cruz
positions.description:
Received NSF funding to sponsor research on smart camera networks. Designed and implemented
smart camera duty cycles on an embedded Linux system. Continued work in the design of server and client software that began during the SURF-IT program. I Designed a mesh networking mode for the same camera network and created an implementation of this system using the Go programming language. (https://github.com/SlugCam/SCmesh)

positions.title: Researcher in Computer Engineering
positions.description: SURF-IT is a NSF sponsored summer undergraduate research program in which I received a grant to contribute to research in the field of computer engineering. In particular I worked in the i-NRG lab and contributed to developing the network software supporting the SWEETcam project.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description: Developed both front and back end components for a web presence built on the Microsoft SharePoint platform. Responsibilities included refactoring legacy code, developing custom SharePoint and ASP components in C#, developing custom utility applications to assist content developers, and front end web development (JS, CSS, HTML). Was also able to assist in a large software system update.

positions.title: Data Entry Assistant
positions.description: Used SQL, Java, and Accelrys Pipeline Pilot to process and load data generated by automated imaging microscopes into a database of research data.

projects.title: micro-signals
projects.description: A small yet flexible signal implementation in TypeScript. Provides convenient transformations on signals for expressive usage patterns.
